If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future. L'IRC met en œuvre des programmes pour promouvoir des solutions durables pour les personnes déplacées, les réfugiés et les communautés d'accueil à travers des projets de santé publique, d'assainissement, d'abris, de réhabilitation et d'éducation. L'IRC est au service des réfugiés depuis 1933 et est présent dans 40 pays d'Europe, d'Afrique et d'Asie, ainsi qu'à travers un programme d'aide à l’intégration aux États-Unis. L'IRC est une organisation engagée pour la liberté, la dignité humaine et l'autonomie. Cet engagement se traduit par une aide à l’intégration bien planifiée, de l’assistance des situations d’urgence dans le monde entier, et du plaidoyer en faveur des réfugiés. La vision de l'IRC pour le Niger est que les individus, les ménages et les communautés soient résilients, autonomes et capables de prospérer dans un contexte en évolution. IRC Niger est présent dans les régions de Tillabery, Agadez et Diffa avec des projets dans les domaines suivants : Santé Environnementale (EH) et Abris et Biens Non Alimentaires (ABNA) y compris avec le Mécanisme de Réponse Rapide (RRM), Protection (SGBV et Protection de l’Enfant), Éducation, Nutrition, Santé et Moyens de subsistance. review_candidates.title: Procurement Officer, Global Procurement (Multi-Category Generalist)
review_candidates.description: The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future. Background The Global Procurement Unit, within Global Supply Chain, leads sourcing strategy, category management, and supplier management for IRC. It is organized around categories, with category owners responsible for sourcing strategy, supplier ecosystem development, and contract and supplier performance across programmatic and corporate spend. Position Overview The Procurement Officer provides procurement execution support for assigned corporate and professional services requests, under the guidance and review of the Senior Manager and relevant category owners. Assignments are limited to an agreed subset of travel, translation, insurance, cash and financial services, and People & Culture services, based on workload and complexity. The officer maintains audit-ready records and supports value for money, timely procurement and compliance with applicable IRC requirements. The Procurement Officer is a hands-on, execution-focused individual contributor supporting assigned sourcing, contract administration and supplier follow-up. The line manager and category owners provide direction and review the officer’s work; category strategy, complex negotiations and award approvals remain with authorized leads. The role enables IRC to move quickly without bypassing procurement controls, vendor due diligence, information security, data protection, legal review, donor compliance, or documentation requirements. The Procurement Officer is the day-to-day procurement focal point for assigned requests and escalates material risks, exceptions, and strategic decisions to the category owner or Senior Manager. Key Responsibilities Category Coverage and Procurement Planning Support assigned sourcing events, renewals and supplier requests from intake to award recommendation, under the guidance and review of the line manager and category owners and in line with agreed priorities. Analyze spend and market data to support demand aggregation and procurement plans for assigned requests, following IRC standard operating procedures and agreed timelines. Support category owners with market assessments and supplier landscape reviews for assigned categories, including ahead of framework renewals, by compiling information on capability, pricing, lead times, risk and total cost of ownership. Provide evidence and options to support category strategy and supplier selection; maintain approved supplier lists and support the establishment of framework agreements under category-owner guidance. Prepare documentation for justified waiver and single-source requests and route them through the required approval process. Sourcing Execution and Negotiation Support requests for information (RFI), proposals (RFP) and tenders by coordinating bidder communications and preparing evaluation records, commercial comparisons and draft award recommendations. Run assigned requests for quotation (RFQ) under the guidance and review of the line manager or category owner and within delegated authority. Help business teams prepare clear specifications, scopes of work and evaluation criteria. Support negotiation of pricing, terms, service levels and performance commitments under the direction of the line manager or category owner and within the agreed mandate. Identify procurement savings opportunities through price benchmarking and competitive sourcing. Calculate and document hard savings and cost avoidance separately against approved baselines, submit them for validation under IRC's methodology, and avoid double counting. Support requesters with procurement intake forms (PIFs) and purchase requisitions (PRs), and create and track purchase orders (POs) in Integra as assigned under approved workflows. Provide procurement documentation for payment requests in ServiceNow, maintaining segregation of duties. Process assigned urgent and emergency procurement requests under approved procedures, using available frameworks where appropriate and documenting required approvals. Follow up supplier milestones and coordinate delivery with the responsible operational teams; escalate delays and capacity constraints to the line manager. Category-Specific Sourcing Support The officer supports a defined subset of the following corporate and professional services categories, agreed with the line manager. Assignments are proportionate to the role’s grade and workload and do not imply responsibility for all categories simultaneously. People & Culture services: support sourcing of recruitment, staffing, payroll, benefits and learning providers, coordinating reviews with People & Culture, Legal and Finance as applicable. Travel: support sourcing and administration of travel provider agreements, comparing rates, fees and service levels with input from the responsible travel and duty-of-care teams. Translation services: support sourcing and administration of translation and interpretation agreements, comparing rates, turnaround times and service requirements with relevant business teams. Insurance: support sourcing and administration of insurance provider and broker agreements, coordinating documentation and specialist reviews with the responsible business owners, Legal and Finance. Cash and financial services: support sourcing of financial service and payment providers with Finance, Treasury and program teams, coordinating required licensing, financial, screening and data protection reviews. Contracting, Framework Agreements and Supplier Performance Prepare contract, framework agreement and statement-of-work drafts using approved templates. Coordinate Legal and specialist review of applicable clauses, route documents for authorized signature, and maintain executed agreements and amendments. Administer assigned framework agreements and contracts: maintain approved price lists, supplier records, expiry and notice dates; alert stakeholders early to renewal needs; and communicate approved terms to relevant requesters and Country Programs. Maintain scorecards for designated suppliers, coordinate reviews according to the agreed schedule and supplier tier, and record agreed improvement actions with business owners. Resolve routine supplier and contract queries within the agreed mandate, escalate material issues, and coordinate follow-up on agreed corrective actions. Liaise with Accounts Payable and requesters on payment delays and report recurring causes. Vendor Due Diligence, Risk Review, and Documentation Coordinate vendor risk assessments and due diligence, risk-based and proportionate to category, value, and data sensitivity: conflict of interest, code of conduct, sanctions, anti-terrorism (ATC) and debarment screening, privacy and data protection, information security, legal, donor compliance, financial viability, implementation risk, and vendor lock-in and exit risk. Track required reviews and clearances with Information Security, Data Protection, Legal, Compliance and Finance before the applicable award or commitment stage. Escalate outstanding reviews; specialist assessments and risk acceptance remain with authorized functions. Identify and escalate requests involving high-risk suppliers, personal or confidential data, AI-enabled tools, client-facing services, or unapproved vendors; for AI-enabled tools, support the application of IRC's AI governance and assessment requirements. Keep procurement files complete, audit-ready, and aligned with IRC sourcing policy and donor requirements, stored in Box; track and follow up missing documentation, approvals, vendor information, and risk reviews; support audit document retrieval. Stakeholder Engagement and Service Support Provide practical, service-oriented support, helping stakeholders move through the process without unnecessary delay while maintaining compliance and risk controls; serve as first point of contact for routine queries and guidance on global vendors and frameworks. Guide stakeholders on procurement routes, required documentation, approval steps, and realistic timelines, and encourage early engagement before commitments are made to vendors. Support the rollout of category sourcing guides, tools, and SOPs, including communication and training materials, and track adoption and gaps. Reporting, Spend Analytics and Continuous Improvement Maintain the sourcing tracker for assigned activities, covering status, cycle time, approvals, risks, documentation and validated benefits. Report progress and recurring intake or requisition issues to the line manager and relevant category owners. Extract, clean and validate Integra data for assigned spend analyses and draft review reports. Report against agreed performance indicators, flag material trends and suggest practical improvements. Identify recurring issues across categories and recommend improvements to frameworks, checklists, templates, and decision tools. Key Working Relationships Internal: Senior Manager, Global Procurement – Corporate & Professional Services; relevant category owners and Global Procurement peers; Global Supply Chain, Country Program and regional supply chain teams; People & Culture; Finance, Treasury and Accounts Payable; travel and duty-of-care teams; relevant business owners; IT and Information Security; Data Protection; Office of General Counsel; Ethics and Compliance; Risk and Compliance; Master Data Management; and other specialist reviewers as required for assigned requests. External: Vendors, service providers, brokers and agencies within the assigned corporate and professional services portfolio; financial service providers; peer humanitarian and development organizations. Qualifications Required Bachelor's degree in procurement, supply chain, business administration, finance, law, or a related field. Equivalent experience may be considered. At least 2 years of procurement or sourcing experience, preferably in corporate and professional services or indirect procurement. Experience supporting competitive sourcing processes (RFQs, RFPs and tenders) and exposure to contract negotiations. Experience coordinating vendor due diligence and compliance risk reviews, including data protection, financial, and operational risk. Proficiency in Excel and ERP or procurement systems; ability to prepare accurate spend analysis and reports. Fluency in written and spoken English, with strong communication skills and the ability to work effectively with internal stakeholders across diverse functions. Strong organizational skills to manage assigned procurement activities and deadlines, identify workload conflicts early, and exercise sound judgment on compliance and escalation. Preferred Professional procurement certification such as CIPS (Level 2 or above), CPSM, or equivalent, completed or in progress. NGO, humanitarian, or donor-funded organization experience, including familiarity with donor requirements such as U.S. Government (e.g. State Department), FCDO, ECHO, EU, UN agencies, or private foundations. Experience in one or more of the assigned categories (travel, translation, insurance, cash and financial services, or People & Culture services), and willingness to develop knowledge of other categories within the agreed portfolio. Experience with Microsoft D365, ServiceNow, Power BI, or similar procurement, workflow, and analytics tools. Experience with contract and supplier performance management, framework agreements, and emergency procurement. Working knowledge of French, Spanish, or Arabic is an advantage. Working Environment Travel of up to 10% domestically and internationally, including occasional travel to IRC country offices. This is a remote position open to internal candidates based in countries where IRC operates who have the right to work in their location. Successful candidates will be hired on a local employment contract and according to local salary scale. This role is open to candidates located and with the right to work in Kenya, Lebanon, and Colombia. Professional Standards: All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. review_candidates.title: Monitoring, Evaluation & Learning Officer - HCI
review_candidates.description: Company Description Founded in 1961, WWF works to help people and nature thrive. As a global conservation organization, WWF operates in more than 100 countries, partnering with communities, companies, and governments to protect wildlife, conserve vital habitats, and advance sustainable solutions. Grounded in science and driven by collaboration, WWF works to help nature by conserving biodiversity, supporting resilient communities, and addressing climate change. Nearly 1 million people in the United States and more than 5 million globally are WWF members. Project Description The Heart of Conservation Initiative ( HCI ) is a 5-year global project designed to address systemic barriers that limit Indigenous Peoples’ and local communities’ ability to steward their lands, territories, waters, and biodiversity-rich ecosystems. Despite strong evidence that Indigenous Peoples and local communities manage or influence at least 37% of remaining natural lands globally, they receive less than 1% of international climate and biodiversity finance, face complex donor procedures, limited direct access to funding, and insufficient recognition in decision-making arenas. Building on the achievements of the GEF-7 Inclusive Conservation Initiative (ICI), HCI’s objective is to increase Indigenous Peoples’ and local communities’ organizational capacities and ability to access sustainable finance at scale for territorial stewardship to deliver social, economic, cultural, and Global Environmental Benefits. The project is transformative in that it targets structural change in biodiversity finance systems—shifting from centralized, intermediary-driven models toward more inclusive, Indigenous Peoples and local community-led financing and governance mechanisms. This will be achieved through four integrated components: (i) organizational and technical self-strengthening of Indigenous Peoples and local community funds and organizations and implementation of self-determined Indigenous Peoples- and local community-led sub-projects across Latin America, Africa, and Asia; (ii) collective self-strengthening of Indigenous Peoples and local community-led funds and organizations’ institutional, fiduciary, and technical capacities; (iii) enhancing Indigenous Peoples' and local communities’ representation and influence in global biodiversity and biodiversity finance processes; (iv) advancing knowledge, learning, and evidence on rights-based, inclusive conservation; and (v) monitoring and evaluation. Job Description LOCATION: This position will be based in Kenya, Cambodia, or Brazil. Major Function Under the guidance and supervision of the Project Manager, the Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning Officer will be responsible for monitoring, evaluation, and learning activities including tracking and reporting project implementation, performance and results achieved – both for C1 partners and the Heart of Conservation Initiative (HCI) as a whole. This is a unique, cross-cutting role (with a focus on components 1 and 5) supporting monitoring of a global, Indigenous-led project that should respond both to Indigenous and local community partners’ priorities as well as GEF core indicator requirements. The MEL Officer will be responsible for the collection and analysis of data in relation to the project activities, outputs, outcomes and impacts; reflecting on and improving the results framework to align with the project theory of change, co-developing a learning agenda and approach, and respond to emerging learning needs and supporting adaptive management; assisting the Project Manager in preparing semiannual, and annual technical reports on project progress; and collaborating with the Communications and Knowledge Management Officer to support identification of impacts and lessons for public-facing communications. The MEL Officer will work in close collaboration with the Project Manager of the Global Coordination Unit (GCU), C1 and other implementing partners, as well as relevant organizations for data-sharing and data management. Key Responsibilities Collaborate with the Project Manager and C1 partners, as relevant, to design methodology for the collection of relevant indicators in close collaboration with all technical specialists. Monitor application of project M&E plans, gather and analyze data for reliability, precision, and feasibility, advising on solutions as needed; and guide usage of monitoring data for project adaptive management, learning needs and decision-making. Deliver a Results Framework and Work Plan Tracking Report for the global HCI at the end of each project year, including, as applicable; measurements against required Core indicators. Co-develop a learning agenda with C1 partners (Indigenous Peoples and local communities’ organizations) – with due focus on Indigenous Peoples and local community-led territorial stewardship and tenure security, Indigenous Peoples and local community-led financing models, women’s and youth leadership in Indigenous Peoples and local communities’ governance, and advocacy in biodiversity finance decision-making fora. Co-develop culturally appropriate learning methods to support the learning agenda and collaborate with project partners to capture lessons learned. Assist the Manager to write the 6-month and 12-month Project Progress Reports/Annual Project Implementation Report for the WWF-GEF Project, including progress, learning and reflections, adaptive management, outcomes, and project ratings. Proactively investigate and reflect on emerging data with C1 partners and GCU staff for adaptive management proposals. Lead planning and organization of the annual reflection workshop to reflect on monitoring data and experience, identify lessons related to the learning agenda and beyond, and inform adaptive management of the project and summarize them in workshop reports. Collaborate with the Gender Equality and Social Inclusion (GESI) and the Communications & Knowledge Management (CKM) Officers to organize and support learning exchanges and knowledge fairs that incorporate and respect traditional approaches to knowledge-sharing among project partners and other relevant parties with emphasis on engaging women and youth. Based on the results frameworks described above, work with the CKM Officer to design a transparent, live database that maintains project monitoring, evaluation and learning knowledge and data collected over the course of project implementation. Support management of said database to ensure data is accurate and updated, with guidance to ensure consistency of measurement methodologies over time. Collaborate with C1 partners and the CKM Officer to respect data sovereignty and address data safety risks through systems, protocols and agreements. Collect and analyze additional data relevant to project from external sources. Troubleshoot challenges with C1 and other partners, including to find culturally appropriate data collection solutions and Indigenous Peoples and local community-accessible reporting and documentation approaches. Contribute to external evaluation planning and execution, including co-design of terms of reference with the Project Manager, C1 partners and WWF GEF Agency, participation in data gathering, review of deliverables, and providing logistical and coordination support to evaluators. Support the Project Manager and CKM Officer to present the project's progress and lessons learned at appropriate regional and international forums. Week-long, international travel may be expected on an approximately quarterly basis. Any other tasks that are relevant to the assignment. Qualifications Key Competencies Demonstrated ability to manage complex, multi-stakeholder projects and competing priorities. Analytical Attention to detail Collaborative Intercultural and adaptive management skills Reliability/follow-through Cross-cultural communication Skills And Abilities A Bachelor’s degree is required in natural or social science, environmental management, program evaluation, international development, adult/organizational learning, or a related field; an advanced degree preferred. At least 7 years of relevant work experience; a Master’s degree in the aforementioned fields will substitute for 2 years of experience. At least 3 of those years of experience must be in the design and implementation of M&E systems for development or conservation projects implemented by national/international NGOs/agencies/government or large, Indigenous associations. Experience supporting Indigenous peoples and local communities organizations with a demonstrated track record of culturally sensitive and respectful, community-centered collaboration with Indigenous Peoples and local communities required. Strong analytical skills/expertise in analyzing data, including expertise using database software, such as Excel or Smartsheet. Experience in research methods, designing and implementing tools and strategies for quantitative and qualitative data collection, analysis and production of reports. Experience using statistical software, such as R or Stata, is desired. Familiarity with the Open Standards for Conservation Management (or WWF Program and Project Management Standards) and results-based management principles, tools, and techniques is preferred. Familiarity with traditional ecological knowledge and biocultural indicators an asset. Experience organizing learning and/or capacity-strengthening events or exchanges, with prior experience supporting learning in international development or conservation an advantage. Strong writing skills and fluency in English required, with Spanish, French, and/or Portuguese fluency or working knowledge strongly preferred. Experience working in distributed teams, ideally across multiple time zones required. International, developing country field experience is preferred, especially in a monitoring and evaluation role in a development or conservation context. Additional Information Location: The position will be based in Brazil, Cambodia or Kenya. If applying to work in Brazil or Kenya, applicants must be nationals currently based and legally authorized to work in Brazil or Kenya. Employment visa sponsorship and relocation are not provided for Brazil or Kenya. If applying to work in Cambodia, nationals from South and Southeast Asian countries who are willing to relocate to Cambodia may also apply, and WWF-Cambodia may be able to support visa sponsorship and relocation costs based on available budget . Please note: Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the job's location. Position is not eligible for employment visa sponsorship. As Energy Vault rapidly grows and delivers on more contracts worldwide, you will build scalable engineering processes, standards, and tools, and feed lessons learned back into our technology and products. Energy Vault operates as both an independent power producer (IPP) and an integrator for customer projects. Your Mission: Lead, mentor, and develop a team of project engineers across the APAC region (Australia & Japan), including hiring, onboarding, goal setting, performance management, and career development.
